title: Mouse meninges isolation for FACS
protocol: Anesthetize mouse with lethal dose of appropriate pharmacological agent.
Perfuse transcardially with ice-cold Perfusion Buffer until mouse is exsanguinated.
Sever mouse head just above shoulders using large scissors.
Carefully detach skin and flesh from skull starting at the caudal aspect, moving rostrally.
Sever eyes at the optic nerve and remove.
Turn head over so that ventral aspect of the jaw is facing up.
Slide angled dissection scissors through the oral cavity until you feel the resistance of the mandibular junction; sever large muscles connecting lower jaw to skull; remove.
Remove lower orbits on each side of the skull using angled dissection scissors.
Use scissors quickly to clean all flesh from aspects of skull.
Make a coronal cut along the suture that defines the most caudal point of the nasal bone with large scissors, preserving olfactory lobes.
Carefully cut shallowly around the skull using tips of angled dissection scissors, leaving brain undamaged; begin and end superior to the external acoustic meatus.
Remove the lower portion of the skull; discard.
Scoop the brain out of the upper half of the skull.
Place both brain and skull-cap in a 50 mL falcon tube with 10 mL ice-cold FACS buffer or suitable cell culture medium, e.g., DMEM-10 or RPMI 1640.
Place brain and skull-cap, with medium, in a petri dish under a dissecting microscope.
Separate the brainstem/cerebellum from the cerebrum with a scalpel.
Hemisect the cerebrum with a scalpel along the longitudinal fissure.
Peel meninges (pia and arachnoid mater) from the surface of the brain, working from medial to lateral.
Remove choroid plexus epithelium and associated leukocytes easily if desired.
Separate the cerebellum from the brainstem; the space between houses the fourth ventricle.
Peel off the ventral aspect of the brainstem in a single section.
Remove the dorsal cerebellar meninges piecewise as with the cerebral meninges.
Score meninges at the rostral-most interior point of the skull-cap using the tip of a Dumont #5 forceps.
Move along the edge of the interior of the skull-cap until meninges are scored 360º.
Peel whole meninges from the inside of the skull if they have been completely scored.
Place a nylon cell screen (70 μm) atop a 50 mL Falcon tube on ice.
Pipette dissected tissue and media directly onto the screen.
Press meningeal tissue with a circular motion (~40x) through the screen using the wide tip of a plastic plunger from a 1 ml syringe.
Pass an additional 20 mL of media through the screen while continuing to mash with the plunger.
Centrifuge at 300 RCF for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Decant the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in the desired medium for downstream applications.
Triturate gently to break up the pellet.
